instruction: Serialize VFX replication packets into a compact buffer in Luau (effect id, position, color, random seed) and decode them on the client.
output:
--!strict
local PACKET_SIZE = 20

local function packVFX(effectId: number, position: Vector3, color: Color3, seed: number): buffer
    local b = buffer.create(PACKET_SIZE)
    buffer.writeu8(b, 0, effectId)
    buffer.writef32(b, 1, position.X)
    buffer.writef32(b, 5, position.Y)
    buffer.writef32(b, 9, position.Z)
    buffer.writeu8(b, 13, math.floor(color.R * 255 + 0.5))
    buffer.writeu8(b, 14, math.floor(color.G * 255 + 0.5))
    buffer.writeu8(b, 15, math.floor(color.B * 255 + 0.5))
    buffer.writeu32(b, 16, seed)
    return b
end

local function unpackVFX(b: buffer): (number, Vector3, Color3, number)
    local effectId = buffer.readu8(b, 0)
    local position = Vector3.new(buffer.readf32(b, 1), buffer.readf32(b, 5), buffer.readf32(b, 9))
    local color = Color3.fromRGB(buffer.readu8(b, 13), buffer.readu8(b, 14), buffer.readu8(b, 15))
    local seed = buffer.readu32(b, 16)
    return effectId, position, color, seed
end

-- Server: remote:FireAllClients(packVFX(3, pos, Color3.fromRGB(120, 200, 255), math.random(1, 2^31)))
-- Client: remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b) local id, pos, color, seed = unpackVFX(b) end)
return {Pack = packVFX, Unpack = unpackVFX}

instruction: Implement a deterministic fractal lightning generator in Luau that uses a replicated seed so the server sends only the seed and every client renders the identical bolt, including branches.
output:
local Debris = game:GetService('Debris')

local function generateBolt(startPos, endPos, rng, iterations, offsetScale)
    local points = {startPos, endPos}
    local scale = offsetScale
    for _ = 1, iterations do
        local nextPoints = {}
        for i = 1, #points - 1 do
            local a, b = points[i], points[i + 1]
            local mid = (a + b) / 2
            local randomDir = Vector3.new(rng:NextNumber(-1, 1), rng:NextNumber(-1, 1), rng:NextNumber(-1, 1))
            local perp = (b - a):Cross(randomDir)
            if perp.Magnitude > 1e-3 then
                mid += perp.Unit * rng:NextNumber(-1, 1) * scale
            end
            nextPoints[#nextPoints + 1] = a
            nextPoints[#nextPoints + 1] = mid
        end
        nextPoints[#nextPoints + 1] = points[#points]
        points = nextPoints
        scale *= 0.5
    end
    return points
end

local function renderPoints(points, folder, thickness, color)
    for i = 1, #points - 1 do
        local a, b = points[i], points[i + 1]
        local len = (b - a).Magnitude
        if len > 0.01 then
            local seg = Instance.new('Part')
            seg.Anchored = true
            seg.CanCollide = false
            seg.CanQuery = false
            seg.CanTouch = false
            seg.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
            seg.Color = color
            seg.Size = Vector3.new(thickness, thickness, len)
            seg.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(a, b) * CFrame.new(0, 0, -len / 2)
            seg.Parent = folder
        end
    end
end

-- Same seed + same inputs => same bolt on every client
local function playLightning(startPos, endPos, seed)
    local rng = Random.new(seed)
    local folder = Instance.new('Folder')
    folder.Name = 'Lightning'
    folder.Parent = workspace

    local mainPoints = generateBolt(startPos, endPos, rng, 5, (endPos - startPos).Magnitude * 0.12)
    renderPoints(mainPoints, folder, 0.35, Color3.fromRGB(170, 210, 255))

    for i = 3, #mainPoints - 2 do
        if rng:NextNumber() < 0.12 then
            local branchEnd = mainPoints[i] + Vector3.new(rng:NextNumber(-1, 1), rng:NextNumber(-0.6, 0.2), rng:NextNumber(-1, 1)).Unit * rng:NextNumber(6, 16)
            local branch = generateBolt(mainPoints[i], branchEnd, rng, 3, 2)
            renderPoints(branch, folder, 0.18, Color3.fromRGB(120, 170, 255))
        end
    end
    Debris:AddItem(folder, 0.2)
end

return playLightning

instruction: Implement a spatial hash grid in Luau for fast radius queries of thousands of moving entities such as projectiles and VFX.
output:
local SpatialHash = {}
SpatialHash.__index = SpatialHash

function SpatialHash.new(cellSize)
    return setmetatable({
        _cell = cellSize,
        _cells = {},   -- [hash] = { [id] = true }
        _items = {},   -- [id] = {pos = Vector3, data = any, hash = number}
    }, SpatialHash)
end

local function hashCell(cx, cy, cz)
    return bit32.bxor(cx * 73856093, cy * 19349663, cz * 83492791)
end

function SpatialHash:_hashFor(pos)
    local c = self._cell
    return hashCell(math.floor(pos.X / c), math.floor(pos.Y / c), math.floor(pos.Z / c))
end

function SpatialHash:Insert(id, pos, data)
    local hash = self:_hashFor(pos)
    self._items[id] = {pos = pos, data = data, hash = hash}
    local cell = self._cells[hash]
    if not cell then
        cell = {}
        self._cells[hash] = cell
    end
    cell[id] = true
end

function SpatialHash:Remove(id)
    local item = self._items[id]
    if not item then return end
    local cell = self._cells[item.hash]
    if cell then
        cell[id] = nil
        if next(cell) == nil then
            self._cells[item.hash] = nil
        end
    end
    self._items[id] = nil
end

function SpatialHash:Move(id, newPos)
    local item = self._items[id]
    if not item then return end
    local newHash = self:_hashFor(newPos)
    if newHash ~= item.hash then
        local oldCell = self._cells[item.hash]
        if oldCell then
            oldCell[id] = nil
            if next(oldCell) == nil then
                self._cells[item.hash] = nil
            end
        end
        local cell = self._cells[newHash]
        if not cell then
            cell = {}
            self._cells[newHash] = cell
        end
        cell[id] = true
        item.hash = newHash
    end
    item.pos = newPos
end

function SpatialHash:Query(center, radius)
    local c = self._cell
    local minX, maxX = math.floor((center.X - radius) / c), math.floor((center.X + radius) / c)
    local minY, maxY = math.floor((center.Y - radius) / c), math.floor((center.Y + radius) / c)
    local minZ, maxZ = math.floor((center.Z - radius) / c), math.floor((center.Z + radius) / c)
    local radiusSq = radius * radius
    local seen, results = {}, {}
    for x = minX, maxX do
        for y = minY, maxY do
            for z = minZ, maxZ do
                local cell = self._cells[hashCell(x, y, z)]
                if cell then
                    for id in cell do
                        if not seen[id] then
                            seen[id] = true
                            local item = self._items[id]
                            local d = item.pos - center
                            if d:Dot(d) <= radiusSq then  -- exact check also filters hash collisions
                                results[#results + 1] = id
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    return results
end

return SpatialHash

instruction: Write a typed config sanitizer in strict Luau that validates untrusted effect parameters from clients (type checks, NaN checks, clamping) before they are used.
output:
--!strict
export type ImpactConfig = {
    Color: Color3,
    Count: number,
    Lifetime: number,
    Radius: number,
}

local function clampNumber(value: any, min: number, max: number, fallback: number): number
    if typeof(value) ~= 'number' or value ~= value or value == math.huge or value == -math.huge then
        return fallback
    end
    return math.clamp(value, min, max)
end

local function sanitizeImpactConfig(raw: any): ImpactConfig
    local source: {[string]: any} = if typeof(raw) == 'table' then raw else {}
    return {
        Color = if typeof(source.Color) == 'Color3' then source.Color else Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
        Count = math.floor(clampNumber(source.Count, 1, 200, 20)),
        Lifetime = clampNumber(source.Lifetime, 0.1, 5, 1),
        Radius = clampNumber(source.Radius, 1, 100, 10),
    }
end

return sanitizeImpactConfig

instruction: Create a data-driven VFX sequencer in Luau: effects are described as timelines of events, played by a single Heartbeat loop with cancel support and error isolation per event.
output:
local RunService = game:GetService('RunService')

local Sequencer = {}
local handlers = {}

function Sequencer.RegisterHandler(name, fn)
    handlers[name] = fn
end

function Sequencer.Play(definition, context)
    local events = table.clone(definition.events)
    table.sort(events, function(a, b) return a.t < b.t end)

    local index = 1
    local startTime = os.clock()
    local connection
    local handle = {}

    function handle.Cancel()
        if connection then
            connection:Disconnect()
            connection = nil
        end
    end

    connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
        local elapsed = os.clock() - startTime
        while index <= #events and events[index].t <= elapsed do
            local event = events[index]
            index += 1
            local handler = handlers[event.action]
            if handler then
                task.spawn(handler, context, event.args or {})  -- one bad handler can't kill the timeline
            else
                warn('[Sequencer] missing handler: ' .. tostring(event.action))
            end
        end
        if index > #events and elapsed >= definition.duration then
            handle.Cancel()
            if definition.OnFinished then
                task.spawn(definition.OnFinished, context)
            end
        end
    end)
    return handle
end

-- Example ------------------------------------------------------------
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local DebrisService = game:GetService('Debris')

Sequencer.RegisterHandler('Flash', function(ctx, args)
    local gui = Instance.new('ScreenGui')
    gui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
    gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
    gui.DisplayOrder = 100
    gui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild('PlayerGui')

    local frame = Instance.new('Frame')
    frame.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
    frame.BackgroundColor3 = args.Color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
    frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
    frame.Parent = gui

    local tween = TweenService:Create(frame, TweenInfo.new(args.Duration or 0.2), {BackgroundTransparency = 1})
    tween:Play()
    tween.Completed:Once(function()
        gui:Destroy()
    end)
end)

Sequencer.RegisterHandler('Shockwave', function(ctx, args)
    local radius = args.Radius or 20
    local ring = Instance.new('Part')
    ring.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
    ring.Anchored = true
    ring.CanCollide = false
    ring.CanQuery = false
    ring.CanTouch = false
    ring.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
    ring.Size = Vector3.new(0.3, 2, 2)
    ring.CFrame = CFrame.new(ctx.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
    ring.Parent = workspace
    TweenService:Create(ring, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Quint, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
        Size = Vector3.new(0.3, radius * 2, radius * 2),
        Transparency = 1,
    }):Play()
    DebrisService:AddItem(ring, 0.6)
end)

Sequencer.RegisterHandler('CameraShake', function(ctx, args)
    local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
    local duration = args.Duration or 0.4
    local intensity = args.Intensity or 4
    local startTime = os.clock()
    local name = 'SequencerShake_' .. tostring(startTime)
    RunService:BindToRenderStep(name, Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, function()
        local alpha = (os.clock() - startTime) / duration
        if alpha >= 1 then
            RunService:UnbindFromRenderStep(name)
            return
        end
        local falloff = (1 - alpha) ^ 2
        camera.CFrame *= CFrame.Angles(
            math.rad((math.random() - 0.5) * intensity * falloff),
            math.rad((math.random() - 0.5) * intensity * falloff),
            0
        )
    end)
end)

Sequencer.RegisterHandler('Debris', function(ctx, args)
    for _ = 1, args.Count or 10 do
        local rock = Instance.new('Part')
        rock.Size = Vector3.one * (0.8 + math.random() * 1.2)
        rock.Material = Enum.Material.Slate
        rock.CanCollide = false
        rock.CFrame = CFrame.new(ctx.Position + Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
        rock.Parent = workspace
        rock.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(math.random(-20, 20), math.random(25, 45), math.random(-20, 20))
        DebrisService:AddItem(rock, 2.5)
    end
end)

local GroundSlam = {
    duration = 1.4,
    events = {
        {t = 0.00, action = 'Flash', args = {Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1), Duration = 0.15}},
        {t = 0.05, action = 'Shockwave', args = {Radius = 30}},
        {t = 0.05, action = 'CameraShake', args = {Intensity = 6, Duration = 0.5}},
        {t = 0.10, action = 'Debris', args = {Count = 14}},
        {t = 0.45, action = 'Shockwave', args = {Radius = 50}},
    },
}

local handle = Sequencer.Play(GroundSlam, {Position = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)})
return Sequencer

instruction: Write a time dilation (slow-motion) system in Luau that scales animation speed and ParticleEmitter TimeScale together and eases in and out.
output:
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local CollectionService = game:GetService('CollectionService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')

local TimeDilation = {}
local current = 1

local function applyScale(scale)
    current = scale
    for _, instance in CollectionService:GetTagged('VFXEmitter') do
        if instance:IsA('ParticleEmitter') then
            instance.TimeScale = scale
        end
    end
    local character = Players.LocalPlayer.Character
    local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
    local animator = humanoid and humanoid:FindFirstChildOfClass('Animator')
    if animator then
        for _, track in animator:GetPlayingAnimationTracks() do
            track:AdjustSpeed(scale)  -- assumes base speed 1; store per-track base speed if you use others
        end
    end
end

function TimeDilation.Slow(scale, holdTime, recoverTime)
    local value = Instance.new('NumberValue')
    value.Value = current
    value.Changed:Connect(applyScale)

    TweenService:Create(value, TweenInfo.new(0.05), {Value = scale}):Play()
    task.delay(holdTime, function()
        local recover = TweenService:Create(value, TweenInfo.new(recoverTime, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {Value = 1})
        recover:Play()
        recover.Completed:Once(function()
            applyScale(1)
            value:Destroy()
        end)
    end)
end

function TimeDilation.Get()
    return current
end

return TimeDilation
-- Tag emitters with CollectionService:AddTag(emitter, 'VFXEmitter'); multiply custom update dt by TimeDilation.Get()

instruction: Write a procedural ground crack effect in Luau that follows terrain with raycasts, uses noise for a jagged path and tapers in width.
output:
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local Debris = game:GetService('Debris')

local function groundCrack(origin, direction, length, segments)
    local flat = Vector3.new(direction.X, 0, direction.Z)
    if flat.Magnitude < 0.01 then return end
    flat = flat.Unit
    local side = Vector3.new(-flat.Z, 0, flat.X)

    local folder = Instance.new('Folder')
    folder.Name = 'GroundCrack'
    folder.Parent = workspace

    local params = RaycastParams.new()
    params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
    params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {folder}

    local lastPos = origin
    for i = 1, segments do
        local alpha = i / segments
        local jag = math.noise(i * 0.7 + 0.3, origin.X * 0.1 + 5.1, 0.3) * 8
        local target = origin + flat * (length * alpha) + side * jag
        local result = workspace:Raycast(target + Vector3.new(0, 10, 0), Vector3.new(0, -30, 0), params)
        if result then
            local pos = result.Position + result.Normal * 0.05
            local segLength = (pos - lastPos).Magnitude
            if segLength > 0.1 then
                local crack = Instance.new('Part')
                crack.Anchored = true
                crack.CanCollide = false
                crack.CanQuery = false
                crack.CanTouch = false
                crack.Material = Enum.Material.Slate
                crack.Color = Color3.fromRGB(15, 10, 10)
                crack.Size = Vector3.new(0.9 * (1 - alpha) + 0.25, 0.1, segLength)
                crack.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(lastPos, pos) * CFrame.new(0, 0, -segLength / 2)
                crack.Parent = folder
                TweenService:Create(crack, TweenInfo.new(2, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.In), {Transparency = 1}):Play()
                lastPos = pos
            end
        end
    end
    Debris:AddItem(folder, 2.5)
end

return groundCrack

instruction: Explain the differences between Heartbeat, PreRender (RenderStepped), PreSimulation and PostSimulation in Roblox and when to use each for gameplay and VFX.
output: PreRender (RenderStepped, client only) fires before each frame is drawn, so use it for camera control, viewmodels and anything that must be pixel-aligned with the camera; keep it light because it blocks rendering. PreSimulation fires before physics runs, so use it to set velocities, forces and character state that physics should react to. PostSimulation (Heartbeat is its alias) fires after physics, so use it to read final positions, run hit detection on resolved physics, and drive cosmetic effects that follow parts. On the server only PreSimulation and Heartbeat/PostSimulation exist. For fixed-rate logic, accumulate dt in PreSimulation and step at a fixed interval, then interpolate visuals in PreRender. Prefer BindToRenderStep with an explicit priority when order against the default camera and control scripts matters.

instruction: Why does network ownership matter for projectiles and physics-driven VFX in Roblox, and how should I handle it?
output: Unanchored parts are simulated by the server or by a nearby client, which is called network ownership. If a client owns a projectile it can manipulate it, so authoritative gameplay objects should be set with part:SetNetworkOwner(nil) so the server owns them, or be simulated manually with raycasts on the server. Purely cosmetic physics (debris, sparks) should be created locally on each client and never replicated. For fast projectiles, avoid relying on physics collisions; step them with per-frame raycasts from previous to current position to prevent tunneling, and have the server decide hits while clients only render the visuals.

instruction: How can I keep VFX identical across all clients without sending every detail over the network?
output: Make the effect deterministic. Send only a small packet: effect id, origin, target and a random seed (or a server timestamp). Every client constructs Random.new(seed) and uses that generator for all randomness (lightning offsets, debris directions, particle counts) and uses workspace:GetServerTimeNow() as the shared clock for timing. Never use math.random inside the effect because it differs per client. This reduces bandwidth to a few bytes per effect, and with buffers you can pack it into about 20 bytes.

instruction: How should I structure a large Roblox project for maintainability and performance?
output: Separate by responsibility and by realm. Keep shared modules (types, config, math utilities, Signal, Janitor) in ReplicatedStorage; server-only logic in ServerScriptService modules loaded by a single bootstrap script; client logic in StarterPlayerScripts modules loaded by one bootstrap. Use a service/controller pattern with explicit Init and Start phases so dependencies resolve before anything runs. Drive content with data (ability definitions, effect timelines) instead of hardcoding, tag world objects with CollectionService and bind components to tags, use strict typing on core modules, and keep RemoteEvent contracts in one place with validators. Use Rojo and git for version control, and add profiling labels around hot paths.

instruction: Find the memory leak in this script and fix it with proper cleanup.
input:
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        local root = character:WaitForChild('HumanoidRootPart')
        local aura = Instance.new('Part')
        aura.Anchored = true
        aura.Size = Vector3.one * 6
        aura.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
        aura.Transparency = 0.7
        aura.Parent = workspace
        game:GetService('RunService').Heartbeat:Connect(function()
            aura.Position = root.Position
        end)
    end)
end)
output:
Problem: every respawn creates a new Heartbeat connection and a new aura, but nothing is ever disconnected or destroyed, so connections and parts pile up for each death. The connection also keeps references to old characters alive.

Fixed version:

local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local RunService = game:GetService('RunService')
local Janitor = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Janitor)

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
    local janitor = Janitor.new()
    janitor:LinkToInstance(character)  -- cleans automatically when the character is destroyed

    local root = character:WaitForChild('HumanoidRootPart')
    local aura = janitor:Add(Instance.new('Part'))
    aura.Anchored = true
    aura.CanCollide = false
    aura.Size = Vector3.one * 6
    aura.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
    aura.Transparency = 0.7
    aura.Parent = workspace

    janitor:Add(RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
        aura.Position = root.Position
    end))
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
end)

local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')

local function hitFlash(character, color, duration)
    local existing = character:FindFirstChild('HitFlash')
    if existing then
        existing:Destroy()  -- restart the flash instead of stacking
    end

    local highlight = Instance.new('Highlight')
    highlight.Name = 'HitFlash'
    highlight.Adornee = character
    highlight.FillColor = color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
    highlight.OutlineColor = color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
    highlight.FillTransparency = 0.2
    highlight.OutlineTransparency = 0
    highlight.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.Occluded
    highlight.Parent = character

    local tween = TweenService:Create(highlight, TweenInfo.new(duration or 0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
        FillTransparency = 1,
        OutlineTransparency = 1,
    })
    tween:Play()
    tween.Completed:Once(function()
        if highlight.Parent then
            highlight:Destroy()
        end
    end)
end

return hitFlash
-- Roblox limits the number of active Highlights; reuse one per character instead of creating many.

instruction: Write a dissolve/vanish effect in Luau that fades every part of a model while shrinking it and bursting particles, then destroys it.
output:
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local Debris = game:GetService('Debris')

local function dissolve(model, duration, color)
    duration = duration or 0.8
    local info = TweenInfo.new(duration, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In)
    local emitted = 0

    for _, descendant in model:GetDescendants() do
        if descendant:IsA('BasePart') then
            descendant.Anchored = true
            descendant.CanCollide = false

            TweenService:Create(descendant, info, {
                Transparency = 1,
                Size = descendant.Size * 0.6,
            }):Play()

            if emitted < 12 and descendant.Size.Magnitude > 1 then  -- cap emitters for performance
                emitted += 1
                local emitter = Instance.new('ParticleEmitter')
                emitter.Texture = 'rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds'
                emitter.Color = ColorSequence.new(color or Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255))
                emitter.LightEmission = 1
                emitter.Size = NumberSequence.new({NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.5), NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0)})
                emitter.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.5, 1)
                emitter.Speed = NumberRange.new(2, 8)
                emitter.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)
                emitter.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(180, 180)
                emitter.Rate = 0
                emitter.Parent = descendant
                emitter:Emit(8)
            end
        elseif descendant:IsA('Decal') or descendant:IsA('Texture') then
            TweenService:Create(descendant, info, {Transparency = 1}):Play()
        end
    end
    Debris:AddItem(model, duration + 1)
end

return dissolve
